summary: Founding sweep, steered six times the same day. The reader clarified that local means fitted to what you have, said they read this as a provider, asked for every team building the loop, and then widened the frame: inference becoming load-aware, how the levers connect, and how to build one. The thesis is now a map of six levers with the agent loop around them. 62 signals are active.

changes.text: The reader answered the two open questions: build the measuring rig first, and the tracker is for building, positioning research and placing a bet. Open ground (six things nobody has shown) added to the big picture. The repository and page were made public.

The reader serves many model families. Churn (C6) joins the claims their position rests on, the provider view now leads with the work that repeats per model, and bringing up a new model is its own step in the build order. W19 opened.
The reader widened the frame to inference becoming load-aware and adaptive, and asked how the parts connect and how to build one. Framing restated; all four parts re-judged.

The big picture: six levers (which model, which machine, the cluster split, decoding, the engine, the model itself), what each listens to and has bought, how they connect through the prompt cache, and a seven-step build order with reusable parts.
Open and frontier models share the work, opened at 0.7. Coexistence is measured on two gateways; whether a router beats a cheap default is disputed.
The model itself becomes a setting, opened at 0.45. Real gains on narrow jobs; tunes go stale and a newer general model beat one.
25 signals for the new levers and the rig, 3 read first-hand. Tensions T7 to T9 and checks W15 to W18 opened.
No longer described as trained on customer traffic. A second check found Modal's other drafter used synthetic data; W15 is to read the post first-hand.
Cadence changed to daily with a weekly deep pass. The repeated procedures (add a signal, act on a steer, roster check, page check) are now playbooks and skills for both agents.

The reader is tracking this as a provider. Added what the evidence implies for a provider, flagged the three claims that position rests on (C4, C7, C3), and opened three provider-side checks (W12 to W14).
The reader clarified that local means fitted to what you have (different devices), not on-device hardware. The framing is restated in those terms and that part now holds.

A roster of every team found that has described the loop: 25 entries with a one-line gist each. A second check found five not seen before (RoofLang, an NPU kernel loop, KDA, FlashVector, Astra); five the first sweep saw and left out are now listed too. Two became signals.
Widened from the workload to what you have: traffic, model and chip together. Confidence unchanged at 0.8.
The on-device claim is retired as out of scope, with five signals that only argued for or against local hardware. Four that show per-device specialisation now count under C2.
Dropped. It was premised on the on-device reading.
W4 and W9 dropped as out of scope. W11 opened: one system showing different winners on two chip families.
Eight claims opened, C1 to C8, each with a starting confidence and named conditions for moving it.
The reader's framing judged for the first time. Workload-aware holds. Local and RSI do not, in the senses those words usually carry.
40 signals: 7 read first-hand, 33 relayed by research sub-agents and marked as such. Relayed ones should be opened and confirmed over the next few sweeps, most load-bearing first.
Six tensions opened. The megakernel split (T1) is the most concrete: two camps shipped opposite bets in the same month.
Ten dated checks opened. The first due is confirming the canonical AgentX scoreboard and recording today's top results as a baseline.
Vocabulary fixed: eight stack layers, five ways an optimisation gets produced, five venues, four timescales, five loop stages.
inference-rsi.com resolved: it is the project page for Evolving Infra (MIT HAN Lab and others, arXiv 2611.12304). Despite the domain, neither page nor paper claims self-improvement.

swept: The five reader-supplied sources and the pages they cite
Agent-driven and self-improving inference optimisation, February to November 2026, including critiques and failed replications
Workload-aware and per-customer serving across providers, open engines and papers
Local runtimes, ML compilers and kernel generation, plus essays for and against local inference
A second check for loop announcements missed: other providers, chip vendors, model labs and the public scoreboard
Model choice: routers, open models inside frontier harnesses, gateway market data, counter-evidence
Domain tuning and speculative decoding that adapts to the workload
Open-source building blocks for the evaluation rig and the adaptive serving pieces
